mr_description:
This commit introduces a new `timeUnit` attribute in the @Scheduled
annotation to allow the user to specify a time unit other than
milliseconds.

expected_issues.title: Duration strings converted to milliseconds, then converted again
expected_issues.description:
parseDelayAsLong() already converts ISO-8601 Duration strings (e.g. 'PT5S') to milliseconds, and the result is then converted again from the annotation's timeUnit, so with timeUnit = SECONDS a 'PT5S' delay becomes 5000 seconds.

Only plain numeric strings are expressed in timeUnit; java.time.Duration strings carry their own unit and are returned in milliseconds by parseDelayAsLong(). Applying TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.convert(value, timeUnit) to both cases multiplies Duration-based delays by the unit factor for fixedDelayString, fixedRateString and initialDelayString. The Javadoc also references non-existent attributes (fixedDelayTimeUnit(), fixedRateTimeUnit()).
